correctness.rationale: The assigned incidence axioms force distance shells (1,q+1,q(q+1),q^2(q+1),q^3) and intersection array {q+1,q,q,q;1,1,1,q+1}; the point-collinearity strongly regular graph spectrum gives adjacency eigenvalues +/- (q+1), +/-sqrt(2q), and 0. As D_p=A1+2^p A2+3^p A3+4^p A4 is polynomial in adjacency, all zero-sum modes are F_q(p), E0=q4^p-(q+1)2^p, and E±=(q-1)2^p-q4^p +/-sqrt(2q)(3^p-1). The written proof proves F_q starts at -1 and increases strictly/convexly, crosses once before b_q=log2(1+1/q), and competitors are strictly negative for p<=b_q by u=2^p-1 <=1/q and 3^p-1<=2u. Centered Gram rank proves endpoint uniqueness and Hilbert dimensions, Taylor expansion F_q(c/q^3) proves the stated two terms along existing q. Independently constructed q=2 GQ incidence distances and eigenmode, plus scalar root checks at q=2,3,5,7,11 confirm finite cases; they do not prove the universal theorem.
residual_risks: For q not realized by generalized quadrangles the formula is not asserted; no weighted/continuous edge generalization.
